name: claude
title: Claude — answer in channels
description: Answers channel cards. Type a message into a card addressed to 'claude' and this runs `claude -p` with the conversation, posting the reply back into the card — so a card can start a turn instead of only being read by an agent you already summoned. Each channel is answered in its OWN project's directory, set in 'Project directories' below; a channel whose project is not listed there is skipped rather than answered from the wrong checkout. With no `claude` on PATH it says so and posts nothing.

config.label: Project directories — one per line, 'Project = /path'
config.help:
Which folder the agent works in when it answers a card, per project. The name on the left is the top-level basket the card lives under, exactly as it appears in the tree; the path on the right is that project's checkout. Example:

  Trellis = /media/veracrypt1/Rust/trellis
  Project5 = /home/null/NodeJS/project5

A card in 'Project5' is then answered by an agent running in /home/null/NodeJS/project5, so 'add a log check to the boot sequence' means that project's boot sequence. Projects not listed here are left unanswered on purpose — a reply worked out in the wrong repository looks exactly like a real answer, which is worse than silence. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.

config.label: Answer automatically (yes/no)
config.help: Default yes. Set to no to stop it running when the document changes while leaving it installed — the Run button in this window still works.

config.label: Fallback directory for unlisted projects (usually leave blank)
config.help: Used only for a channel whose project has no line above. Blank — the default — means such a channel is skipped and says so in the log, which is normally what you want. Set this only if you have a single project and would rather not name it.

config.label: Give up on one reply after (seconds)
config.help: Default 240. A turn running longer than this is abandoned and reported in the log; nothing is posted to the card, and the message is answered again on the next change.

config.label: Most messages to answer in one run
config.help: Default 3. A guard: an import or a paste can put many messages into channels at once, and every answer is a real model call that costs money. The rest wait for the next change.
